chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin and Abu Ayoub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who said to his wife, 'O adulteress, I have committed adultery with you,' he (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is one Hadd (penalty) for slandering her, and as for his words,
I have committed adultery with you,
there is no Hadd (penalty) in it, except if he testifies against himself with four testimonies of adultery in the presence of the Imam.
ai.seo_question: What is the Hadd penalty for a husband who calls his wife an adulteress and claims he slept with her?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between the fixed penalty for slander (Qadhf) and the evidentiary requirement for self-incrimination in adultery cases. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that a husband's claim of adultery with his wife does not automatically incur the Hadd penalty unless he formally testifies to it four times before the Imam, emphasizing the procedural rigor required for such severe penalties.
